articles.title: FACEIT Developer Blog: IEM Rio on FACEIT Watch
articles.body:
IEM Rio 2024 has arrived! We continue improving your CS2 viewing experience on FACEIT Watch ! Our commitment to delivering the best for our community drives us to build new features and improvements that make your engagement with esports even more exciting.

Since the beginning of FACEIT Watch , we’ve been dedicated to building a more interactive way to enjoy content, featuring multi-POV options that let you watch up to four player perspectives and a main map POV for real-time strategy analysis. You can earn valuable skins and FACEIT Points just by tuning in to your favorite events, instant access to VODs for catching up on past matches with multiple perspectives, and the convenience to easily clip and share legendary plays from any player’s POV on social media.

With IEM Rio just around the corner, we’re excited to show you some updates and features designed for you:

New Chromecast capabilities: We’re super excited to share that you can now watch FACEIT Watch on your TV with our new Chromecast capabilities , which will be available in beta for IEM Rio! This means you can kick back and enjoy all the action right from your living room or Android TV. With access of up to 2 POVs on the Chromecast version. To learn more about the Chromecast feature and how to use it, check our support article .

We’ve been hard at work refining FACEIT Watch. Here’s what’s new:

New CDN in Asia: A new CDN mirror has been deployed in Singapore, improving video streaming performance for our Asian users. This change, implemented on September 12th, ensures faster load times and smoother playback.

Miniplayer: Lets you keep watching your favorite content even when you leave the watch tab. Seamlessly viewing videos while navigating through other tabs on FACEIT.

Video Player Updates: Redesigned controls for easier navigation, including new buttons, volume controls, and a seek bar.

Support was added for playing streams on iOS devices.

Bug fixes including proper seeking in multiview and improved mobile support with double-tap-to-seek functionality.

Game Insights: The highlight feature will now deliver the most accurate, current information when you subscribe.

Chat: We now have a character limit for chat messages. Also some bug fixes including improved chat icon performance and crash fixes.

Backend Improvements: View-count tracking for VODs is now available, so you can see how many times content has been watched.

Stability improvements: in game stats and bug fixes related to score tracking and highlights.

Join us on FACEIT Watch starting today for all the action live from IEM Rio!

Feel the adrenaline, earn exclusive rewards, and relive epic moments. If you need to catch up on previous games, don’t forget that FACEIT Watch VODs are already live and ready for you!

articles.title: Introducing the Overdrive Cup!
articles.summary: Last February, we launched the WASB Cups, a weekly tournament aimed at giving Overwatch teams of all skill levels the opportunity to train…
articles.body:
Last February, we launched the WASB Cups, a weekly tournament aimed at giving Overwatch teams of all skill levels the opportunity to train in official competitions. The goal was to improve their Elo and secure better seeding for OWCS and FACEIT League.

The WASB Cup allowed many teams to progress while also earning substantial rewards. Since its launch, the WASB Cup has seen:

More than 3,600 players participated in over 2,800 matches

$15,000 and over 18 million FACEIT Points distributed

In today’s blog, we will give you all the details about the Overdrive Cup , our brand new weekly tournament designed to help organized teams improve and sustain their careers.

The WASB Cups are gone, long live the Overdrive Cup!

Since their launch in February, we haven’t made any major changes to our weekly tournaments. With the Overdrive Cup , we wanted to revitalize the weekly cup concept, making it more appealing to players, while also helping teams of all skill levels improve throughout the week to enhance their performances in FACEIT League and OWCS.

This new initiative offers a fresh approach with attractive prizes and a live-streamed finals event, designed to give up-and-coming teams and grassroots players the opportunity to gain exposure within the community, as well as a new way to make their teams financially sustainable over time.

A free competition, using OWCS and FACEIT League rules, available in NA / EMEA / SA and OCE

Prizes that support teams in their ambition to become sustainable and break through in the competitive scene, with $2000 to be won each month and more than 2 million FACEIT points to be shared monthly

A multi-stage experience, featuring weekly tournaments leading up to the finals

Monthly Finals streamed by the community in multiple languages to provide greater visibility for teams and identify grassroots talent

Content creator teams will be invited to the Monthly Finals to boost the visibility of your team, but also to give you the chance to compete against big names in the community

Whether you are from NA , EMEA , SA or OCE , sign up now and experience our brand new Overdrive Cup! We hope this fresh format helps you refine your skills and strategies for FACEIT League and OWCS, while also setting you on the path to making your team sustainable, so you can launch into the high-level Overwatch scene.

As always, we’re excited to hear your feedback and answer any questions you may have, so don’t hesitate to join us on FACEIT Overwatch Discord .

As we continue to improve our competitions and the experiences we bring to Overwatch players on FACEIT, we’ll be back soon with announcements on exciting new features. In the meantime, we look forward to seeing many of you in the Overdrive Cup and wish you the best of luck in winning your matches!

articles.title: Two New NA Servers, Unlocking Nicknames, and Bringing a Touch of Anime to FACEIT in our October…
articles.summary: As we move into November, we’re back again with the last set of Patch Notes… for the FACEIT platform as you know it. Luckily, that’s the…
articles.body:
As we move into November, we’re back again with the last set of Patch Notes… for the FACEIT platform as you know it. Luckily, that’s the only spooky news we have for you this month, with positive changes to our NA server pool and tournament plugin to talk about instead! We’ve also included some long-awaited shop features, such as the anime collection out this month, and the ability to claim your nickname from an idle player coming soon! It’s been a pleasure to share how we’re improving FACEIT for you these past few months, and we’d love to know what you liked (or didn’t!) about our patch notes, so do let us know !

Play with better ping with new East and West Coast NA servers

We’re still working hard on connection issues based on your feedback , but we’re also picking up your feedback, and testing the impact of adding a wider variety of server locations! We’ve begun this effort by adding two new test server locations to NA matchmaking in San Jose and Virginia : aiming to provide better options for west and east coast players respectively looking for a server closer to home. To allow you to play in a more convenient location and test out the new servers, we’re still only requiring you to select 2 servers, out of a pool of 5 (previously 3). While this may increase queue times, we wanted to give you the flexibility to play with low ping should you choose, and the option to add other servers in the pool for shorter queue times remains available! As this is a test period, we’re especially eager to hear back from you about your experience, so let us know what you think!

Idle Nicknames soon purchasable in the FACEIT Shop!

The wait is nearly over! Soon, nicknames held by inactive accounts will finally be available for others to purchase. We understand how important your nickname is to you, so we’ve built in protections to prevent abuse or accidental loss. To begin with, a nickname will only be released after 12 months of account inactivity. Additionally, these inactive players will receive an email one week in advance, reminding them that logging into FACEIT resets the 12 month timer. To further protect this feature, nickname claiming is a FACEIT Premium perk, though free users can purchase it for $4.99 or 5000 FACEIT Points in the Shop. Premium users can claim a new username for free every three months. Plus, if your nickname is claimed, you’ll receive 1000 FACEIT Points — enough to choose a new one if you decide to return!

Level Up Your Style: Avatar Frames & Anime Collection available for purchase

You asked, we delivered! Avatar Frames are now live on FACEIT Shop, ready to be paired with your favorite Profile Cards or used solo to create striking, funky vibes. Choose between two designs — static (Circuit) and animated (Voltic) — both available in our debut FACEIT Collection in six vibrant colors. Just like Profile Cards, Avatar Frames show up not only on player profiles but also on play, matchroom, and league pages across FACEIT. Grab your favorites using FACEIT Points or your local currency.

That’s not all though! Recently, we introduced our latest release: the Anime Collection ! This limited-edition set features six unique Profile Cards and six epic Avatar Frames, each designed to bring a fresh, anime-inspired feel to your profile. Whether you’re into serene, dark, or explosive vibes, you’ll find the perfect combo to suit your style. Keep in mind that these are going fast, so don’t wait too long to secure your favorites.

Added !DHLDrops to FACEIT Watch streams… at the click of a button!

Released PoV sharing: you can now send your FACEIT Watch configuration for a stream or VOD with a shareable link!

Tidied up the layout of the homepage and VOD pages

Fixed a bug where 2 volume sliders would appear

The missions widget on the matchmaking screen can now display multiple missions

Added a player-sided round restore functionality — togglable by Organizers

Any team member can now select a side after winning a knife round if the team’s captain is not on the server instead of only the captain being able to select a side

Adjusted the automatic No-Show AFK forfeit logic to grant the win to the team with the most members present on the server

Moved the substitution phase to start after the map and server vetoes are finished. Previous: Match Scheduled -> Substitution (Lineup confirmation, if a team has substitutes) -> Server Veto -> Map Veto -> Match Ready New: Match Scheduled -> Server Veto -> Map Veto -> Substitution -> Match Ready

Added notifications for various Team roster management events

Added a two-step confirmation before banning a user from a League roster to prevent accidental removals

Added an option to view combined Standings from all of Leagues stage’s conferences

Added more detail to error messages when attempting to make roster changes

Added a “Go to Matchroom” button on the League overview page when the player is in a scheduled League match

The Player’s League division is now shown on their user profile under “Game Stats”

Updated the design of the Season Records panel on a user profile

When using “Find Team,” clicking on a team will now open an in-app modal instead of opening the team page in a new window

When using “Find Team,” Teams now have a “Copy Link” button above their Team roster panel

Team roster panel now has a “Make Officer” button visible for each player, only visible to the Team’s captain

Team Officers now have an icon in the Team roster panel

Bugfixes & Quality of Life improvements:

Added a notification when successfully updating rules on tournaments

The game registration panel now shows in a tournament header before joining

Middle-clicking on the “Team details” button on a roster modal now opens the team page in a new window instead of redirecting the user to it in the same tab

On Team pages, the Leagues participation history is now displayed in chronological order, sorted by most recent first

Tournament participants’ tabs now use infinite scroll pagination instead of a “Load more” button

Fixed a bug where registrations were not reopened after reopening signups on a tournament

Fixed a bug with Double elimination tournaments where it was not possible to disable double finals or change the number of slots

Fixed a bug where Swiss-system tournaments would get stuck generating rounds

Fixed a bug where it was not possible to disqualify a participant if the team had been already eliminated

Fixed a bug where copying a championship from the Organizer page would not work

Fixed a bug where teams were getting removed from tournaments after checking in

Fixed a bug where not-yet-started matches would show “STARTED NAN MINS AGO” on the Matches tab of Championships

Fixed a bug where some players in a Team roster would not appear on the “Manage Roster” panel

Fixed a bug where a league roster was available in the sidebar for players that were not part of the roster

articles.title: FACEIT Matchmaking Season 3 wraps up with yet another victory for donk!
articles.summary: It’s been another four thrilling months of Counter-Strike as amateur and pro players alike race for that coveted top spot on the FACEIT…
articles.body:
It’s been another four thrilling months of Counter-Strike as amateur and pro players alike race for that coveted top spot on the FACEIT Matchmaking leaderboards and their share of $100,000, as well as bragging rights and a stamp for up-and-coming players to show on their esports passport. Once again, donk has proven to be truly inevitable in his path to yet another victory, racking up a total of 5075 Elo — even more than he accrued last season!

The young prince of Counter-Strike hasn’t relented one bit this season, and racked up over 200 extra Elo this time round to firmly place himself at the very top once again! With a gap of 223 Elo over his next-closest contender and a third consecutive triumph over the rest of the world, what will it take to dethrone him? The task certainly isn’t easy: with a 69% win rate over 357 matches this season, bolstered by an impressive suite of stats, it would take an equally prodigal talent to even come close!

Want to know what it takes to play at donk ’s level, even against the best players in the world? We’ve got the recipe:

First, mix together the key ingredients to make sure your firepower is up to scratch:

Make sure to sprinkle in 10 knife kills and 1 Zeus for extra style, and maybe then you’ve got what it takes to challenge him!

While donk may have been too much to handle once again, the rest of the EU region has fought hard for their share of the prize money, with kyousuke from Spirit Academy and m0NESY from G2 rounding out the top 3 for a particularly young podium — the future of Counter-Strike looks scarier than ever!

NA After coming second last season, dea has claimed the top spot this time round, making a statement by blazing nearly 200 Elo ahead of Peeping and alter , who have both climbed 3 spots over their Season 2 placement — can one of them go all the way next time?

SA In South America, it’s pepe ’s turn to be crowned our champion, narrowly edging out Misfit to clinch the top spot and proving his worth as an up-and-coming talent, while clon7 closes out the podium. No other region has seen their leaderboard shaken up so much since last season: with only pepe and kye managing to keep their place among the top 10, who knows who the next champion may be?

On the other side of the world, our Asian leaderboard has been topped by Sange with 3978 Elo, followed by Anasasis and Crunchy

Meanwhile, the boys at SemperFi have locked up the entire Oceanic podium! shadiy leads the way with an impressive 4688 Elo, while his teammates keen and vision round up the top 3 in a true show of force for the team.

Over the next week, we’ll be handing out top 1000 badges to all winning players once correctly reassigned to the region they’ve played the most matches in this season — congratulations on your hard-earned prize!

That’s a wrap for FACEIT Matchmaking Season 3! We’re looking forward to Season 4, which is just around the corner with new heights to reach, fresh competition, a new Elo reset on season start and a couple surprises for you all coming later this month… Stay tuned to find out more!

articles.title: Overwatch Champions Series: 2025 Season
articles.summary: In 2025, OWCS will build on the foundation of 2024, where we created a more open ecosystem that culminated at international Live Events at…
articles.body:
In 2025 , OWCS will build on the foundation of 2024, where we created a more open ecosystem that culminated at international Live Events at DreamHack in Dallas and Stockholm.

Entering the 2025 Season, we are focused on making competition more rewarding for competitors and viewers alike through an intuitive & streamlined esports program with three international Live Events.

Read below to learn more about the OWCS 2025 Competitive Season and how FACEIT League now directly promotes to NA & EMEA OWCS.

2025 Format - Live Events - NA & EMEA Format - Asia Format - Eligibility

FACEIT League now qualifies for OWCS in NA/EMEA

Opening Weekend, Stage 1 Schedule, & Viewership Incentives

The OWCS 2025 Season offers a more streamlined & cohesive international format, supporting competition across three competitive stages.

Each stage will feature Regional Competition leading into that stage’s international Live Event.

Depending on the Stage, our three regions of NA, EMEA, & Asia will each host an (a) Open Qualifier or Promotion & Relegation Tournament, from which Teams will qualify into the (b) Regular Season, where Teams will compete for a spot at their (c) Regional Playoffs. Each Regional Playoffs will determine which Teams get the opportunity to represent their region at each Stage’s International Live Event.

Partner Teams will auto-qualify for Stage 1 Regular Season, but can be relegated like all other Teams during Promotion & Relegation Tournaments going into Stages 2 & 3.

Here is how the 2025 season breaks down;

Stage 1 [January to April 2025] - Regular Season - Regional Playoffs - Promotion & Relegation (Stage 2) from FACEIT League - Live Event [TBD]

Stage 2 [Q2 to Q3 2025] - Regular Season - Regional Playoffs - Promotion & Relegation (Stage 3) from FACEIT League - Live Event

Stage 3 [Q3 to Q4 2025] - Phase 1: Regular Season - Phase 2: Regional Playoffs - OWCS 2025 World Finals

Head here to read more on the 2025 OWCS Ruleset. (Please note that the rules will be available soon, and all dates are subject to change.)

In the 2025 season, OWCS will be ditching circuit points, with teams qualifying for each of our three international Live Events directly through their region’s playoff performance.

Stage 1 culminates with our first international Live Event, with competition from top teams across all OWCS. articles.title: Community Showdown is back and it’s bigger than ever!
articles.summary: Community Showdown is back and bigger than ever!
articles.body:
Community Showdown is back and bigger than ever!

The first edition of the Community Showdown was a massive success, with over 20 tournament organizers bringing their communities together to claim a share of the $5,000 USD prize pool and more than 2 million FACEIT Points. Leading community names from around the globe joined the showdown, with over 400 teams participating, featuring teams from Ex Oblivione, Battletech, Grupo Senju, and many other communities, the tournament crowned Team Shikigami from the Overwatch Season community and Team Schweppes from the Hammerkick community as respective champions of the NA and EMEA regions.

Community Showdown is one of the largest Overwatch community competitions of 2024, and this second iteration promises to be even grander!

Benefit from the best Platform for your tournaments!

Staying true to our promise to the Overwatch community, we’re offering all select approved third-party tournament organizers free access to our platform’s infrastructure, enabling them to host and manage various tournament formats sustainably, easily, and efficiently. This allows organizers to engage their communities better than ever, while empowering Overwatch teams and players with consistent, rewarding, and aspirational content that extends beyond OWCS and FACEIT League events.

Selected third-party tournament organizers (you can apply here ) will automatically and freely receive:

A streamlined OW license request process, facilitated by FACEIT: FACEIT will now handle Blizzard license approvals on your behalf for hosting events on FACEIT. Simply apply through this link , and we’ll be in touch with you shortly with the outcome.

A seamless tournament experience for your tournaments: No more manual configurations! FACEIT allows you to smoothly manage every aspect of the match lifecycle (mode, map, side, and server selection) and report all results and stats back to the platform at the end of each match.

Easy onboarding with 24/7 support: Our experienced support team is here to guide you, ensuring you can offer the best competitive experience possible to your community.

More rewards for your community: Tournament organizers participating in Community Showdown II will offer 100,000 FACEIT Points as additional tournament prizing. FACEIT Points are our in-house currency, enabling your community to purchase Overwatch cosmetics, Overwatch Coins, and other products available in the FACEIT Shop .

Amplified communication for your events: To ensure the success of your events, you’ll benefit from exposure across FACEIT X , Instagram , TikTok , Organizer page , and Discord channels, maximizing your reach to attract even more players.

The opportunity to continue hosting your own tournaments after Community Showdown II: We’re thrilled to announce that select approved tournament organizers can keep using FACEIT’s integration with Overwatch, alongside our support, to run your own events for your community, providing them with the ultimate competitive experience.

Don’t wait — submit your application to host your tournaments here !

Introducing Community Showdown II with $7,500 and 3 Million FACEIT Points up for grabs

Starting 7th of December 2024, communities will compete across a variety of tournaments to secure a slot in the Community Showdown finals, taking place on 4th and 5th of January 2025. In total, $7,500 USD and over 3 million FACEIT Points are up for grabs for the participating teams. Here’s what to expect from Community Showdown II:

Selected third-party tournament organizers will host tournaments in their preferred format, qualifying their top teams for the $7,500 Community Showdown II finals.

100K FACEIT Points will be awarded to each organizer to support their tournament’s prize pool.

Each organizer will have the freedom to stream their competition, support co-streams, and create content on their channels without any restrictions.

Following our preliminary discussions with tournament organizers, we’re pleased to confirm the participation of the following communities.

Don’t miss out — join Community Showdown II by submitting your application here .

Join Community Showdown II, showcase your community, and host your tournaments on FACEIT!

We invite all community leaders eager to participate in Community Showdown II to apply now to host a tournament and benefit from the FACEIT platform and all of its advantages. Don’t miss this unique opportunity to bring your community consistent and recurring competitions throughout 2025 and beyond.

If you have any questions, feel free to reach out via email anytime at: organizers@faceit.com

Overwatch tournament organizers, we hope to see you soon on Community Showdown II!

articles.title: Climb to OWCS in FACEIT League Season 4 with multiple new improvements!
articles.summary: Don’t miss learning from the best Master teams as they battle for their share of $50,000 and glory with Season 3 playoffs this weekend…
articles.body:
Don’t miss learning from the best Master teams as they battle for their share of $50,000 and glory with Season 3 playoffs this weekend streamed here !

Gain more competitive experience as you enjoy new improvements for FACEIT League Season 4 including:

Start your climb to OWCS with FACEIT League

Earn your share of $800,000 with $200,000 just for tier-2 teams with 4 FACEIT League seasons in 2025

Find new friends who want to see how far they can go with our “ Find Team ” feature for Season 4

Helping fit League officials around your busy schedule with improvements including simultaneous offers, proposal history, and notifications when your opponents reply

Making our settings more Overwatch-specific by adjusting the veto and roster selection process

Understand League more easily with an updated season page

Learn more below about how your competitive Overwatch experience has been leveled up in Season 4!

If you missed the OWCS World Finals in Stockholm, here’s a quick recap. Other than wild strategies, world-class players, and passionate fans, we announced FACEIT League’s connection to OWCS ! Now, anyone can start their esports journey in the Open division and work their way to Overwatch’s most prestigious competition!

To help balance the divisions and make sure everyone starts competing at a level appropriate for their skill, there’s multiple free qualifiers at the start of next year so you can fast-track your competitive journey!

$200,000 for tier-2 teams with four seasons in 2025

We also announced a full year of competition for amateur teams competing for a minimum of $50,000 per season outside of OWCS. We guarantee four seasons of competition so teams have a consistent schedule of weekly official matches to look forward to. Instead of waiting months between qualifiers, teams can now work toward OWCS while still improving their skills.

This also includes prizes and competition for South America and Oceania where we hope to build the foundation in 2025 with active teams funding more opportunities for competitive players using the League Pass membership.

With FACEIT League registration closing in January, an incredible 350 teams have already started registering for Season 4 to see if they can climb to OWCS. With that, some teams don’t have a full team of 5 ready, just yet!

Don’t forget that you can use our “find team ” feature to browse teams who want to find players to gain competitive experience with! Join their teams and use the chat to coordinate when to play. You’ll get notifications in our FACEIT mobile app to easily stay on top of these for less time organising and more time practicing.

We are also aligning the FACEIT League roster size with OWCS so teams may have a maximum of 7 players and 1 coach. Keep in mind teams can still add up to 3 players per 7 days before the Roster Lock in case they need an emergency substitute.

Helping fit League officials around your packed schedule

It could be a real struggle to organise League matches around College, work, or other competitions. We’ve focussed on scheduling for Season 4 with multiple improvements to make it easier to find the time to join more competitive matches.

Avoid wasting time going back and forth with your opponents with times they won’t accept as we now highlight when you offer a proposal that was previously rejected. You can now offer multiple times simultaneously so your opponent can choose from several proposals at the same time. For example, if you can play multiple times on the same day or at the same time each night.

You can communicate faster with your opponents rather than writing in chat and hoping they notice the message as we’ve introduced “reasons” for rejecting an offer to communicate a specific response, eg “we can’t do Tuesday”. Finally, if your circumstances change, you can reject your own offer so you don’t need to worry if your opponents will accept the time.

It is now easier to stay on top of your League scheduling when away from your PC with notifications when offers are sent, accepted, or rejected. These notifications are sent using email, the bell at the top of the screen, and now the FACEIT mobile app .

During Season 3, we updated our process for both selecting rosters and how they would be displayed to make them more aligned with Overwatch.

For example, instead of players deciding who “starts”, at the beginning of each match teams will pick who is “red”. Similarly, instead of picking players before the map, at the start of a multiple-game series, teams will now pick their 5 players after the map has been selected. This way they can swap in any substitutes for that specific matchup.

As we continue to expand in Overwatch, more players who are less familiar with esports will be joining the platform. We have updated our season page so it is easier for you to understand how to join and start climbing to OWCS!

Good luck in Season 4 as you climb to OWCS through the skill-balanced division, gaining experience in weekly official matches, that are balanced around your schedule!

articles.body:
Take your first step into competitive team play to earn your first Valve Regional Standings Points with ESEA League kicking off on January 8th! Compete in weekly official matches, against teams of your skill, and based around your schedule!

Get a taste of the unforgettable League atmosphere with multiple experience improvements, including:

A path to your first Valve Regional Standing Points by restructuring ESL Challenger League

Fairer officials with Open10, Open9, and Open1–8 in Europe and Open9–10 and Open1–8 in North America

Better placing Open teams using the average Elo rather than levels

Making sure you have time for League games with improvements including multiple scheduling offers when your opponents reply, offer history, and mobile/email notifications

Prepare for the season and see how far you can go in Fast-Track qualifiers

Improve your skills by exploring detailed statistics diving with our new Track feature

Building more trust with verification for all Advanced regular season matches

A clearer way to register with the League page updated to help you understand how to compete

Supporting grassroots with the Middle East Open on Dubai servers providing a consistent competitive schedule, promoting to EU Main

A path to your first Valve Regional Standing Points in ESEA League

Instead of endlessly grinding FACEIT, competitive players want high-pressure officials to earn their place at the top rather than hope they get noticed by an established organisation. Fans are inspired watching the next jL, ZyWOo, or donk, burst onto the scene after rising through the lower divisions.

This is a core reason for Counter-Strike’s success. articles.title: FACEIT Watch Update: IEM Katowice, Chromecast, and More!
articles.body:
IEM Katowice is here, and we’ve got some massive updates to make your FACEIT Watch experience even better! Whether you’re tuning in from your TV, phone, or desktop, we’re making sure you catch all the action your way!

Sidebar Scroll Issue — The left-side ‘matches’ menu no longer has unwanted horizontal scrolling when collapsed.

FPL Map Display Issue — The ‘view details’ section in the matches menu now correctly displays the map being played.

As always, we love hearing your feedback and can’t wait for you to try out these new updates. Tune in to IEM Katowice on FACEIT Watch and let us know what you think!

articles.title: $7 million! AG.AL crowned Esports World Cup 2026 club champion after landmark Paris edition
articles.summary: Esports News: AG.AL were crowned Esports World Cup 2026 club champions after a dramatic final weekend in Paris, securing the $7 million (~INR 66.9 crore) top prize .
articles.body: AG.AL were crowned Esports World Cup 2026 club champions after a dramatic final weekend in Paris, securing the $7 million (~INR 66.9 crore) top prize following seven weeks of record-breaking esports action featuring more than 2,000 players, 200 Clubs and 25 tournaments across 24 games.AG.AL finished on 5,300 points, edging two-time defending champions Team Falcons, who ended runners-up with 4,600 points. Team Vitality finished third with 3,300 points, followed by Natus Vincere (2,950) and Team Liquid (2,700).The club championship went down to the wire, with AG.AL completing their campaign through Gwendal âGwenâ Duparc's victory in the inaugural Trackmania tournament. The Frenchman delivered under pressure to win the tournament and secure the club championship for AG.AL.Falcons had entered the Trackmania playoffs at the top of the overall standings, but Carl-Antoni âCarl Jr.â Cloutier's quarterfinal exit opened the door for AG.AL. Gwen then dominated the final, securing the $130,000 (~INR 1.2 crore) tournament prize and, more importantly, the club championship.AG.AL's title-winning campaign also featured a first-place finish in Tekken 8, second-place finishes in Chess, Free Fire and the Honor of Kings World Cup, and a third-place finish in Teamfight Tactics.AG.AL complete remarkable campaignâWhen we began expanding AG.AL globally in 2024, the same year the Esports World Cup launched, we set out to build a Club capable of succeeding across games, regions and cultures. This title shows how far that vision has come,â said Eddy Chen, COO at AG.AL.âOur journey in Paris reflected the strength of the entire organization, from M. Zubairâs breakthrough in TEKKEN 8 and our deep runs across multiple titles to Gwen delivering the decisive Trackmania victory under extraordinary pressure. But this trophy belongs equally to every player, coach and staff member whose dedication brought us here.âThe Paris edition also produced several memorable individual performances. France's Caliste âCalisteâ Henry-Hennebert led Karmine Corp to the League of Legends Grand Final in front of a home crowd, while 15-year-old Chilean Jaime âCraimeâ Bustos became the youngest Esports World Cup champion after defeating two EVO champions.AG.AL's Khawaja âM. Zubairâ also captured the Tekken 8 title, while Rocket League star Samy âdraliiâ Hajji became the first three-time Esports World Cup champion. Grandmaster Magnus Carlsen successfully defended his Chess title without losing a game.Paris delivers record numbersThe 2026 edition set new benchmarks for the Esports World Cup, with the event reaching 850 million viewers and generating 440 million hours watched â increases of 13% and 26%, respectively, year-on-year. Peak viewership reached 4.3 million during the League of Legends tournament.The event was distributed globally through more than 100 broadcast and OTT partners in 47 languages, with 5,000 creators and co-streamers supporting its coverage.In another major milestone, 175,000 tickets were sold for esports competitions, a 94% increase from 2025. Total visits across competition venues, Fan Fest and city activations exceeded two million during the seven-week event.âWe are proud of what the Esports World Cup has achieved in Paris and of its continued international growth,â said His Royal Highness Prince Faisal bin Bandar bin Sultan al Saud, Chairman of the Executive Committee of the Esports Foundation.âBringing the EWC to a global audience beyond Saudi Arabia marks an important milestone in its journey and reflects the growing recognition of esports as a global industry, connecting communities, cultures and audiences around the world.âParis was the first city outside Riyadh to host the Esports World Cup. More than 22,600 campaign placements across the capital reached 94% of Parisians, while the final weekend's Counter-Strike tournament was staged at the 20,000-seat Accor Arena.The event followed a year-long competitive journey involving more than 1.5 million players across 330 Road to EWC events.âOur ambition has always been bigger than a single event: to grow esports and establish it as a leading global sport,â said Ralf Reichert, Chief Executive Officer of the Esports Foundation.The Esports World Cup will return to Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, in 2027.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: El inesperado torneo que decide la cuarta plaza de Premier Padel
articles.standfirst: Yanguas y Nieto jugarán el FIP Gold de Belgrado, en el que también están inscritos Stupa y Sanz
articles.summary: Yanguas y Nieto jugarán el FIP Gold de Belgrado, en el que también están inscritos Stupa y Sanz
articles.body: Hace semanas se anunciaron las dos nuevas parejas que se formaban tras las rupturas del P1 de Londres. Mike Yanguas volvía a juntarse con Coki Nieto, mientras que Franco Stupaczuk pasaba a competir al lado de Jon Sanz. Todo apuntaba a que los españoles serían los que arrancarían como cuartos en el ranking por una distancia mínima, pero la cancelación del Major de Qatar ha provocado que se cambien los papeles, obligando a estas dos duplas a pelear por ese privilegiado puesto en el FIP Gold de Belgrado que se celebra esta semana. Cuando se unieron, Yanguas y Coki figuraban como cuartos en la lista de inscripciones del P1 de Madrid, superando por tan solo 21 puntos a Jon y Stupa. Esa posición permite evitar a los principales candidatos al título hasta semifinales, dejando un camino mucho más asequible sobre el papel. Una ventaja que el motrileño y el madrileño esperaban mantener, pero que se ha visto alterada por un condicionante inesperado. Premier Padel suspendió la prueba prevista en Doha en el mes de abril. Se trata de la cita que más puntos reparte, la cual fue sustituida por Kuwait, torneo que tendrá lugar en noviembre. Sin embargo, existía un problema con los puntos de 2025, que debían restarse precisamente con la disputa del Major de Qatar. Al no haberse celebrado, la organización optó por restar de manera progresiva el resultado conseguido la pasada temporada. Por tanto, aunque no haya torneo en juego, los jugadores continúan perdiendo esas unidades semana a semana. Mike y Nieto alcanzaron las semifinales en la edición anterior, mientras que Jon solo llegó a cuartos. Stupa, por su parte, no pudo ni siquiera participar por problemas físicos. Esta circunstancia ha provocado que los primeros hayan descontado más puntos desde su unión tras el P1 de Londres hasta la fecha, dejando a Franco y Sanz en la cuarta plaza por 55 unidades; una situación que ni siquiera los propios protagonistas conocían de antemano. “Mi objetivo con Franco era recuperar la cuarta plaza. Él me llamó pensando que íbamos a ser quintos y hace un par de días me enteré de que seríamos cuartos en Madrid”, explicó el drive navarro en Padel Addict. Con la pugna en un margen tan estrecho, ambas parejas se han inscrito en el FIP Gold de Belgrado. Se trata de una prueba de la quinta categoría del circuito internacional (por debajo de Major, P1, P2 y FIP Platinum) que otorga 150 puntos a los ganadores. Un botín que supondría un intercambio de posiciones de cara al Major de París, dado que el P1 de Madrid ya cerró sus inscripciones con Jon y Stupa como cuartos cabezas de serie. Así pues, lo que ocurra en tierras serbias determinará quién llega con ventaja a Roland Garros. Ambas duplas parten como las principales candidatas al título, ostentando la condición de cabezas de serie uno y dos de la cita. También figuraban inscritos Aimar Goñi y Edu Alonso, aunque finalmente no acudirán. Por el lado de Yanguas y Coki, Álex Ruiz y Javi García se perfilan como la mayor amenaza, mientras que Jon y Stupa se cruzarían en su camino con duplas como Jofre-Bautista o Xisco Gil-Pablo Lijó. En cualquier caso, todo apunta a un hipotético cruce en la final para definir la cuarta plaza en París. No obstante, si Sanz y Stupaczuk no alcanzan la ronda definitiva, les valdría con que Mike y Nieto no levanten el título para mantener su posición. Una batalla que se librará semana a semana y que marcará el arranque de estos dos nuevos proyectos en la élite.

articles.title: 'No major damage' for Forfar player after game abandoned for neck injury
articles.summary: Forfar Athletic say Adam Livingstone has not suffered any major damage after Tuesday's Challenge Cup match against Formartine United was abandoned because of...
articles.body:
Forfar Athletic say Adam Livingstone has not suffered any major damage after Tuesday's Challenge Cup match against Formartine United was abandoned because of a neck injury suffered by the defender.

Forfar led 1-0 when Livingstone was hurt in an aerial clash early in the second half.

He received treatment on the pitch and was subsequently taken to Ninewells Hospital in Dundee, where he stayed overnight.

"Following last night's injury, Adam was taken to Ninewells Hospital where X-ray results have not shown any major damage," Forfar said in a statement on Wednesday.

"Adam was kept in hospital overnight but we have been advised that, all being well, he should be allowed home later today."
